### LOW: Debug file\-derived cache KEK is not in the threat model, which still says the KEK is SE\-rooted
[docs/architecture/security/encryption\.md:113](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/23eb9d3776482dd73963c810f7ba3b92a8ccbb61/docs/architecture/security/encryption.md#L113) · T-041

The new text at encryption\.md lines 110\-118 documents a DEBUG\-build path \(\`DARKBLOOM\_DEBUG\_CACHE\_KEY\_FILE\`, \`SSDDebugCacheKeyFile\.swift\`\) that derives the SSD cache KEK from an on\-disk file\. It also documents an explicitly allowed ephemeral\-key mode for ad hoc signed builds\. The file\-derived key is protected only by ownership, mode 0600 and volume encryption, not by the Secure Enclave\. T\-041 and its mitigations still treat every key as SE\-rooted: K\_lookup is derived from the SE\-rooted KEK, a KEK wipe is the cryptographic purge, and lookup names are unfindable without the KEK\. A key file that is readable, copied or backed up lets a disk observer or operator recompute the HMAC lookup tags and decrypt DBK3 files\. That would reopen the leak \#2 class that the HMAC design closed\. The claim that release builds do not contain this path rests on code not supplied here, so the exclusion is unverified\. Fix: update T\-041 to record the debug and ephemeral KEK modes and the tag\-recomputation and decryption exposure from the key file\. Also state the build\-time exclusion from release artifacts as a mitigation with a verification reference, such as a release\-binary symbol check\.
